frequency_question: How often do historical actions matching the substantive intent of penalizing major foreign banks for prohibited commodity trade successfully meet the specific formal written criteria of official Treasury department announcement and financial system cutoff within a tight 35-day window?
membership_rule: Members are defined as announced escalations where the executive branch targets major foreign commercial banking entities for trade with sanctioned jurisdictions. Excluded are vague warnings, unannounced private diplomatic demarches, or sanctions targeting small tier-3/tier-4 institutions rather than major commercial banks.

cases.name: Kunlun and E.D. Commercial Bank designations under NDAA

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major named precedents representing all primary historical instances of major foreign bank financial restriction announcements by Treasury.
known_gaps: Minor informal warnings or shelved designations that did not reach official implementation are outside the counted set.
skeleton: Named historical precedents of major foreign bank penalty announcements divided by total major target enforcement actions meeting formal Treasury announcement criteria.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 documented major formal enforcement actions where the substantive policy intent to penalize was executed within the formal criteria parameters.
validity_reason: Treasury statutory authorities and announcement mechanisms for secondary banking sanctions remain stable across administrations.
